title: A stem that stands on its own
statement: Write each stem as a full question that names everything it asks students to relate, so that a student who knows the material can answer it with the options covered.
example: An item with no question in it passed even the judge that noticed, at 0.88.
detail: The AP generator's item checklist asks for a stem understandable without reading the options, and its guidance answers stem ambiguity by reviewing stems before options are added (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/analysis/best_practices.md`). A cross-review found an item with no question stem at all, which both model judges passed (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/CLAUDE_CROSS_EVAL_REPORT.md`). A review of generated questions listed comparisons with one side missing among its clarity issues, and a judge failed a part for a vague region label (`icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/python/docs/EVALUATION-RESULTS-2026-02-23.md`; `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_results/unit_1/diagnosis.md`). The writer rules require naming both things compared (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/generators/saq.py`). Write it as a question, not a sentence to complete.
